content.text: I've reviewed the grant of rights, definitions, shared resources, miscellaneous, termination, and the sales/marketing exhibit. No restrictive covenant binds Corio.

input.quote: 13.6 Independent Development: Covenant not to Sue. Nothing in this Agreement will be construed to prohibit either parties' right to independently develop the Developments contemplated above.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Corio. Section 2 (p0030-p0045) grants only non-exclusive licenses and contains no promise by Corio to refrain from hosting, building, buying or reselling competing e-procurement products; Section 2.7 (p0042) is a standard IP/scope restriction (no copying, reverse engineering), not a market restriction. Section 13.6 (p0117) expressly preserves each party's right to develop independently, and Section 14.8 (p0131) confirms Corio solely directs and may subcontract the Corio Services. The "CORIO MARKET SEGMENT" (p0013) and "TERRITORY" (p0024) constructs, and the Customer definition (p0019), operate as the scope of the licenses Commerce One grants to us rather than as covenants limiting the businesses we may operate — Section 2.10 (p0045) even lets us push the geographic scope worldwide with consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and p0016 permits us to keep serving customers that grow past the revenue threshold. Exhibit D (p0197-p0205) is expressly "non-binding" sales and marketing cooperation, so it imposes no enforceable market limitation. Nothing survives termination as a post-term restraint (p0098). No redline required.
